newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: U.N. envoy dismayed by Najibullah hanging.
newsitem.headline: U.N. envoy dismayed by Najibullah hanging.

text.p: U.N. peace envoy for Afghanistan, Norbert Holl, on Friday expressed "deep dismay" at the execution of former Afghan president Najibullah and his brother by Taleban militia and public display of their bodies.
In a statement issued in Islamabad, he appealed for sparing the lives of two remaining companions of Najibullah, a bodyguard and his former chief of staff, now in Taleban hands.

Holl, who heads the United Nations Special Mission to Afghanistan (USMA), said armed men abducted Najibullah and his brother Shahpur Ahmadzai from the USMA compound in Kabul in the early hours of Friday and later killed them.

He said the abduction of the former president and his companions and the subsequent killings "without any legitimate judicial procedure" constituted a grave violation of the immunity USMA premises enjoyed under international law.
These acts "also further jeopardise all the efforts which are being made to secure a peaceful settlement of the Afghanistan conflict," Holl said.
"USMA deeply deplores these tragic events, which cast a doubt over the willingness of those responsible to achieve reconciliation and guarantee justice in the area controlled by them," he said.
"USMA appeals with the utmost gravity to those responsible to spare the lives of Dr Najibullah's two remaining companions."
Holl praised the former president for making "a considerable contribution" to the peaceful transfer of power to the Mujahideen guerrillas after 14 years of civil war in April 1992.
"In recognition of this, the secretary-general of the United Nations granted him and his companions protection in USMA's premises in Kabul for over four years," he said.

"Throughout this time, and in particular in recent days, the United Nations have made strenuous efforts, for humanitarian reasons, to find a solution to the case of Dr Najibullah, with a view to enabling him to return safely to his family," Holl said.
He said Najibullah had "formally abjured any political activity in the future."

The bodies of Najibullah and his brother were seen by witnesses hanging from a concrete traffic-control post at the gates of the presidential palace as a crowd of more than a thousand people crowded around to watch.
"We killed him because he was the murderer of our people," Noor Hakmal, a Taleban commander who entered the city from Charasyab, south of Kabul, overnight, told Reuters.
The Taleban entered Kabul in tanks and on foot overnight on Friday, meeting little resistance from government forces which had abandoned the city hours before.
The Islamic movement announced just hours after the takeover that an interim six-man ruling council would run the country.
